_comment: Fragment 19 — D-62, FR-14 written, G60 closed. Merged 2026-08-20.

nodes.label: FR-14 — Business-Continuity Observability Surface
nodes.description: Present a business-continuity surface displaying the defined critical observations, each with its current value and when it was last evaluated. P1, S3, Line 2. Carries US-14 and AC-21, plus a §7.2 Project Scope row and NFR-05 and NFR-08 coverage. Closes G60.
nodes.rationale: Written into Modular_PRD because D-29 places tier two as the owner of new capabilities; inventing it in Fn_Specs would have put a requirement at the wrong tier. Deliberately narrow: it displays observations existing requirements already define and introduces no new measurement, threshold or alerting, which keeps it a compensating control rather than a capability with its own scope.

nodes.label: Team-Added Scope Is Disclosed, Never Absorbed
nodes.description: FR-14 has no Customer Request origin. It exists because the Chief Editor attached C-13 to D-57. It is therefore recorded in the §7.2 Project Scope Matrix alongside FR-11 through FR-13, which carry the same disclosure, rather than attributed to a CR that did not ask for it.
nodes.rationale: The discipline FB-03 established when the Line filter was added to the board. Attributing team-added scope to an existing CR would make the customer appear to have requested something they did not, and would hide the growth of scope inside a requirement that already had approval.

nodes.label: AC-21 — Never Observed Must Not Render Blank
nodes.description: A condition never yet observed must read not observed, never blank. An empty reading is indistinguishable from a healthy one: a surface showing nothing for escalation backlog could mean no escalations exist, or that the check never ran.
nodes.rationale: G41's rule applied one tier out, from the audit surface to the continuity surface. On a continuity surface the two readings demand opposite responses, so conflating them is worse than showing nothing at all.

nodes.label: Three AC Tables, Three Shapes
nodes.description: Section 9.1 Functional carries six columns including AT source; 9.2 Non-Functional and 9.3 Security carry five. AC-21 was first written into 9.3 and moved to 9.1 after a column-count check against neighbouring rows.
nodes.rationale: Seven rows carrying five columns initially looked like seven malformed rows. They were a different table, not a defect — the naming-difference error family in structural form, avoided by checking the shape before naming it. The column-count check is what caught both the real placement error and the false one.
